records.name: Imaginary Lines
records.summary: An artist collective that shows artists' work through exhibitions and film screenings, runs creative writing workshops with immigrant communities, and collects stories from people through a share form.
records.what_you_do: Send a story through the Share Your Story form, or email the collective to ask about showing work or screening a film. The group also runs creative writing workshops with immigrant communities in Philadelphia and other cities, and its site says workshop participants are paid for their time and creative work.

cost.text: Cost is not listed on the site for sharing a story or writing in.

first_step.how: Send a story through the Share Your Story form on the site, or email the collective to ask about a workshop or to pitch an exhibition or screening.
first_step.basis: Anyone can send a story through the public form or write by email, and the site describes no membership or application. The site does not describe how to join a workshop.

records.notes: The site is thin. The Share Your Story page does not say what the form asks or what happens after a submission. The contact and support pages carry no dates. The newest dated item found is a 2024 honor on the artists page (MICA Animation Festival), so probably_active may be generous and the owner may want to recheck status. Tier1 cost was 'free' without a source for it; now unknown. The contact page writes the email address in words; recorded here in standard form. The support page links a GoFundMe donation page, not recorded.

records.name: Independence Seaport Museum
records.summary: A museum at 211 S. Columbus Blvd with historic ships and boats. Its docent program trains volunteers to lead tours of the museum and its ships, but it is not taking new applications right now.
records.what_you_do: Docents lead tours of the museum and its historic ships, help with education programs, and welcome guests at special events. Other volunteer areas on the site are helping restore the historic ships Olympia and Becuna, working in the J. Welles Henderson Research Center, and assisting master boat builders at the Seaport Boat Shop.

schedule.text: Docent tours run year round on weekdays and weekends. Docent training is four required sessions in late February and early March.

cost.text: The required background and child abuse clearances are free and completed online after you apply.

first_step.how: Docent applications are closed for now. Call 215-413-8655 or email seaport@phillyseaport.org to ask when the volunteer program reopens.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says the museum is at maximum capacity for volunteers and is not accepting applications, so there is no open way in right now.
first_step.what_to_expect: Docent applications are closed, so there is no volunteer first visit to plan right now. If the program reopens, expect a free online Pennsylvania background check and child abuse clearance before your first day, then four required training sessions in late February and early March. The museum itself is open Thursday through Tuesday, 10 am to 5 pm, with the last entry at 4:30 pm and closed on Wednesdays.
first_visit_tips: Start the Pennsylvania background check and child abuse clearance early, since both must be received before your first day, with no exceptions.
Clearances obtained in Pennsylvania within the last 12 months are accepted.
The museum is closed on Wednesdays and the last entry is at 4:30 pm, so plan your visit around those times.

records.notes: The volunteer program is closed to new applications as of 2026-10-08 (at maximum capacity, no waitlist information). The verdict stays publish because the museum itself is open to visitors, but the owner may want to decide how to show the closed volunteer program. The volunteer page gives no time commitment and no physical access details, and names no SEPTA stop, so access and nearest_septa are left out. The email seaport@phillyseaport.org is listed on the accessibility page for accessibility questions; it is recorded as a contact, and the owner may want to confirm it is a general address. The training sessions have no year on the page, so none is written.

records.name: IndependentSounds
records.summary: A festival of opera and instrumental music that started in Philadelphia in 2023. Shows run an hour or less, and voice students of all levels can perform onstage with professional singers and an orchestra.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to see the festival's performances, or join the email list to hear when the next season opens. Voice students can perform with the festival, though the site does not say how to sign up.

schedule.text: An annual summer festival of opera and instrumental music, usually running several days.

cost.text: Tickets are sold for each performance. The site does not list prices or pass options.

first_step.how: Join the email list on the site to hear when the next festival season opens, then buy a ticket for a performance.
first_step.basis: The about page says the shows are aimed at first-time audiences as well as longtime fans, and the home page offers a ticket purchase and an email list as ways in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each show is one hour or less, and foreign-language productions include English translations. You buy a ticket for one performance, and the venue changes from year to year, so check the address on your ticket. Ticket prices are not listed on the pages we could read, so check the sales page before you go.
first_visit_tips: Some past shows were held in private homes, with the address given only on the ticket after purchase.
If you sing and want to perform, ask the festival directly, since the site does not describe how voice students apply.

records.notes: The tickets page returned 404 and the shows page is an archive of the 2025 festival, so ticket prices and pass options are not established. The 2026 venue (Performance Garage) and the August 7 to 9 dates come from a WRTI article found by the one web search, not from the group's own site. Past venues: a private home in 2023; St. Clement's Church parish hall in Philadelphia and a private home in Bryn Mawr (outside the city) in 2025. Crowd changed from all_adults to all_ages because the about page says it welcomes people of all ages. The newcomer rating of 4 rests on the about page's first-time audience wording plus the ticket and email ways in.

records.name: Indigenous Peoples' Day Philly Inc
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit working to make Indigenous Peoples' Day a permanent city holiday. It holds a public celebration each October and runs cultural, educational and community-building programs.
records.what_you_do: Take one of the posted volunteer roles, such as a general volunteer, an internship, writing or design help, or a campaign assistant role. You can also attend the October celebration, subscribe to the newsletters, or join, donate, or sign the petition through the website.

schedule.text: A public celebration held each October at Shackamaxon (Penn Treaty) Park. The holiday falls on the second Monday of October.

cost.text: Admission to the celebration is not stated on the site. The website has ways to donate, join or subscribe.

first_step.how: Come to the public October celebration at Shackamaxon (Penn Treaty) Park, or apply for a posted volunteer role through the form on the volunteer page.
first_step.basis: The celebration is public, and volunteer roles are posted with an application form. The site gives no orientation or welcome steps for first-time volunteers.
first_step.what_to_expect: The October celebration is held at Shackamaxon (Penn Treaty) Park, where the group has put it on since 2019. Volunteer roles run three to six months, from about two to six hours a week, and most are open to Indigenous Peoples and allies.
first_visit_tips: Send questions about a volunteer shift through the contact form on the website before you start, since no orientation is listed.

records.notes: The events page returned 404, so no dated community meeting list was found. The tier1 mention of campaign community meetings is not confirmed on the deeper pages, so it is left out of the summary and what_you_do. The join page says most opportunities are open to Indigenous Peoples and allies, that volunteer positions are for Native Americans and allies, that board seats are for Lenape, Native American, Indigenous or Indigenous-descent people, and that presenting at the annual celebration is for Native Americans only. The site does not say in those words that attending the celebration is open to anyone; the public celebration wording comes from the tier1 read, so confirm. Days 'mon' come from the holiday rule and the 2026 celebration date. The office mailing address on the about page is not a meeting place and is not in locations.

records.name: InLiquid
records.summary: A Philadelphia art group with a gallery at Crane Arts that shows local artists' work, runs an online magazine and posts calls for artists.
records.what_you_do: Visit the gallery Wednesday to Saturday, come to artist receptions (RSVP through the links on the site), apply for artist membership, or submit work to its calls for artists. The site also lists workshop calls, such as a Saturday glassblowing workshop, and no volunteer roles.

schedule.text: The gallery is open Wednesday to Saturday, noon to 6 pm. The Crane Arts office is open weekdays from 10 am to 6 pm, by appointment only.

cost.text: Gallery admission and artist membership fees are not listed on the site. The site has donate links.

first_step.how: Visit the gallery on a Wednesday to Saturday afternoon, or RSVP for an evening reception through the links on the site.
first_step.basis: Gallery visits and receptions are open to the public through the site. Artist membership needs an application.
first_step.what_to_expect: Gallery visits take place in afternoon hours at Crane Arts, where you can look at the current show on your own. Receptions are evening events with the artists, and some shows also have artist talks, with RSVP links on the site.
first_visit_tips: RSVP through the link on the site for receptions.
Crane Arts is at 1400 North American Street, and the gallery is Gallery 108.

records.notes: The membership, artist-membership and about pages returned 404, so artist membership fees, eligibility and deadlines are not established. Tier1 said gallery visits are free and that the site lists no classes. The site does not say visits are free, so that claim is removed. A Saturday glassblowing workshop appears in the calls list with an October 17, 2026 deadline; who may attend is not stated, so it is not called a public class. The next gallery show is Let's Begin in the Middle, October 23 to November 28, 2026, per the homepage. Other partners named on the homepage (Cheltenham Center for the Arts, 20/20 Photo Festival, Park Towne Place, Hyatt Centric, Old City Publishing) have no website link read, so they are not in leads_only.

records.name: InterAct Theatre Company
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater company that develops and stages new and contemporary plays at The Drake, and takes in new scripts from playwrights.
records.what_you_do: Buy single tickets or a season subscription to see the plays, join the mailing list for show news, or submit a script. The company also offers post-performance talk backs and free public convenings and symposia. The site lists no volunteer or usher roles.

schedule.text: Runs a season of new and contemporary plays each year at The Drake, with run dates posted on the site.

cost.text: Single tickets are $20 to $49. A season subscription is $120. Student and senior discounts are not listed on the site.

access.notes: Icons on the ticket page list wheelchair seating, a listening option and front-row seats, with no further detail.

first_step.how: Buy a single ticket for the current show through the box office or the website, or join the mailing list for show news.
first_step.basis: Single tickets are sold to anyone through the box office and website. The site describes no first-visit welcome and no volunteer way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: You buy a ticket and watch a professional production in the Proscenium Theatre at The Drake, on South Hicks Street in Center City. Single tickets run $20 to $49, and a season subscription is $120. Post-performance talk backs are part of the company's programs, so ask the box office whether one is planned for the show you choose.
first_visit_tips: Call the box office at 215-568-8079 or email boxoffice@interacttheatre.org about wheelchair or front-row seats before you buy.
The Drake is at 302 South Hicks Street in Center City.

records.notes: Wheelchair access is recorded as yes on the basis of the wheelchair icon in the ticket page's accessibility section, which gives no further detail; the owner may want to confirm it. Audio description, ASL and relaxed performances are not described on the pages read. The Outreach page returned 404, and the about page gives no detail on outreach or education. The about page gives no founding date. Resident companies at The Drake (PlayPenn, Simpatico Theatre, Azuka Theatre, Inis Nua Theatre Company) and the National New Play Network are named with no website link read, so they are not in leads_only. Schedule text stays general on purpose, since run dates are dated items.

records.name: Inti Media
records.summary: A media organization that makes news, films and podcasts with a focus on Black and Latin American communities. Its news sections are in English, Spanish and Portuguese, and community members can pitch story ideas.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer to help with stories, pitch a story idea, attend a community pitch meeting, or sign up for the monthly newsletter. You can also come to community events such as a Spanish-language film club and a monthly Afro-Latin dance lesson and social.

schedule.text: A Spanish-language film club meets most Tuesdays, 6 to 7 pm. A monthly dance lesson and social runs on Sundays at FDR Park, 12 to 4 pm. Community pitch meetings are held each season.

locations.label: Mercado Latino at FDR Park (dance lesson and social)

cost.text: The dance social is free with no RSVP. No fee is listed for volunteering, pitch meetings or the newsletter, and donations are optional.

first_step.how: Come to the monthly Sunday dance lesson and social at the Mercado Latino at FDR Park, or email production@intimedia.org to offer help or pitch a story.
first_step.basis: The dance is free with no RSVP, and the site gives an email address for volunteering and story pitches. The site describes no training for new volunteers.
first_step.what_to_expect: The monthly Sunday dance starts with a one-hour lesson, then becomes a social until 4 pm, and it is free with no RSVP. The site says the dance is open to LGBTQ+ people. Community pitch meetings are held each season and are open to everyone.
first_visit_tips: Ask the group for the exact meeting spot at the Mercado Latino at FDR Park, since the events page gives no street address.
Email production@intimedia.org to offer a story idea; the site does not describe what a pitch should include.

records.notes: The events page lists dated events from April to October 2026, which is the basis for last_sign_of_life 2026-10. The Sunday dance is listed as open to LGBTQ+ people, which is reflected in what_to_expect; the community audience (black, latino) is kept from tier1. The April 30, 2026 pitch mixer at Our House Culture Center was a one-off and is not in the record. The events page lists both production@ and productions@; the record uses production@, which the footer and get-involved page give. Philadelphia Documenters, a paid training program that the events page lists as relaunched in August 2026, may deserve its own record; not checked. Partner groups named on the events page with their own websites, Taller Puertorriqueño (tallerpr.org) and Centro Integral de la Mujer Madre Tierra (madretierraphilly.com), were not fetched in this pass and are not in leads_only. Newcomer rating is 3 because the page does not describe a first-time welcome, although pitch sessions are open to future collaborators. The about page returned 404.

notes: Used 26 page fetches (8 returned 404, none were bot checks or 403s; no rate limiting) and 1 WebSearch (IndependentSounds 2026 venue and dates, from a WRTI article). Two points for the owner: Independence Seaport Museum's volunteer program is closed to new applications, so its newcomer rating is 1 and the record says so; Imaginary Lines may be less active than tier1 said, because its newest dated item is a 2024 honor. Tier1 corrections are explained in each record's notes (InLiquid free-visit claim removed, IndependentSounds crowd changed to all_ages, Imaginary Lines workshops added from its support page). Leads: Taller Puertorriqueño and Centro Integral de la Mujer Madre Tierra have their own websites but appear only on the Inti Media events page; they were not fetched in this pass and are dropped for this wave, with the reason given in the Inti Media record. Partners named without a website link (PhillyCAM, PA Humanities, Cheltenham Center for the Arts, 20/20 Photo Festival, PlayPenn, Simpatico Theatre, Azuka Theatre, Inis Nua Theatre Company, National New Play Network, Fleisher Art Memorial, Esperanza Arts Center, Our House Culture Center, TCCW, ArchWell Health, Brandywine Workshop) are not listed because no URL was read.
